text:
ana: Heads-up — the dedicated canary rollout for rook-dedicated (us-east) shows a big tail latency regression after last night's release. p95 token latency ~2x on long-seq workloads. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/p/rook-dedicated/canary
raj: Noted. p50 is fine, it's the p95/p99 tail that jumped. Any KV-cache churn or batching changes in the merge?
mei: I started a profiler sweep. Early signal points to kernel-selection heuristics picking a different matmul kernel for shapes we see in long sequences. Also seeing KV cache miss rate up ~7% on the canary tenant logs.
jordan: CI perf ran and reported +8% on the perf-suite but it didn't cross the alert threshold so pipeline passed. This explains why it shipped.
ci-bot: perf-suite: run/1798765000 - test=long_seq_p95 +60% vs baseline (threshold +75% required to fail)
nana: I'm bisecting now, suspect the heuristic change in the runtime commit sequence around 47b2f12 -> 9a3c4e0. Will report the first failing commit.
raj: quick grep shows kernel-priority code touched in 47b2f12 (runtime/kernel_selector.cc). That commit added a short-seq bias to prefer fused kernels. Could cause suboptimal picks for long sequences.
mei: local revert of that function fixes p95 on our repro harness (long_seq_4k tokens). Patch diff is small.
nana: command I used:
```
git bisect start HEAD base/2026-03-10
git bisect good base/2026-03-10
git bisect bad HEAD
# bisect pointed to 47b2f12
```
raj: Important: the change also altered batching heuristics slightly (batching/window growth). If kernel selection + batching interact badly we can get cache eviction patterns that amplify latency.
mei: profiler flamegraph excerpt (trimmed):
```
- attention_forward
  - matmul_generic (hot)
  - fused_matmul (cold)
- kv_cache.lookup (increased misses)
```
ana: Customer impact: the dedicated tenant rook-42 saw sustained p95 > SLA (SLA p95 < 300ms, observed ~650ms for token steps during peak). We're in SLA risk territory. Sales/CS pinged.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-03-12-17 - "dedicated canary p95 regression" :eyes:
jordan: Options:
- hotfix: revert kernel-priority commit (fast, regresses some short-seq perf)
- config toggle: expose runtime.force_kernel_policy=legacy for canary/dedicated (non-invasive, immediate)
- rollback full release (big blast radius)
ana: I prefer config toggle first so we can flip without revert. Can we ship a config-only patch?
raj: I can prepare a small runtime flag PR to force legacy policy. That should be low-risk. Will include a test that asserts kernel selected for our repro shape is "legacy_matmul".
mei: once flag is in, I'll run canary in us-east and run the long_seq perf harness. If results look good we can roll forward the flag to affected dedicated pools.
jordan: I'll prepare the rollback playbook in case toggle doesn't work. Also notify Dedicated ops and account team for rook-42.
nana: PR checklist:
- raj: open PR with flag + config binding
- mei: perf run + flamegraphs before/after on canary
- jordan: customer comms + rollback plan
- ana: hold release for other regions until canary is green
raj: opening PR now: https://internal.redwood/p/runtime/PR-9001 (WIP)
ci-bot: build/9001 started - linux/gcc - unit+integration
mei: quick note — if we expose the flag we should also add telemetry to track kernel selection distribution (kernel_id + seq_len histogram) to verify behavior in prod.
nana: Agreed. Add a short-term metric: runtime.kernel_selector.choice_count and runtime.kvcache.miss_rate per tenant.
raj: PR posted, tagged @mei @jordan for review. Targeting hotfix canary windows in 30m.
nana: If canary looks good, we flip flag on rook-dedicated groups; otherwise we revert the release. Timebox 2h for investigation+canary.
jordan: I'll DM CS with the mitigation plan and ETA.
mei: Running canary perf now. Will post results in ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(20m later)
mei: Canary results: p95 back to baseline (~280ms), kv cache miss down to previous baseline, kernel choices show legacy_matmul dominating for long shapes. Looks good.
nana: Great. Flip to affected dedicated pools, monitor for 1h, then consider a safer reintroduce of heuristic after more testing.
raj: Rolling config to rook-dedicated-1/2/3 groups. Patch also includes a metric.
sre-bot: rollout to rook-dedicated-1 started at 1798765725
sre-bot: rook-dedicated-1 health OK, rook-dedicated-2 started at 1798765740
sre-bot: rook-dedicated-2 health OK, rook-dedicated-3 started at 1798765760
ana: Thanks team. Follow-ups:
- deeper perf investigation: batch-size x kernel interactions (mei)
- revisit kernel-priority heuristic with more shapes + perf-suite thresholds (raj)
- CI perf thresholds review to catch this earlier (jordan)
- CS update sent, ticket INC-2026-03-12-17 updated with root-cause and mitigation
ana: closing this thread once the 1h monitor window passes. :white_check_mark:
